literal: The friendship of those who resemble kin but are not kin, like the mind of women, will become different.
translation: The friendship of those who pretend to be your kin but are not, will constantly shift and change like the minds of fickle women.
modern: உறவினரைப் போல நடித்து, உண்மையில் உறவினர் அல்லாதவர்களின் நட்பு, பெண்களின் மனத்தைப் போல மாறிக்கொண்டே இருக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet warns us about the unstable nature of false friends. The poet describes them as people who outwardly act like our own kin ('inam pōṉṟu') but are actually not ('inam allār'). Their friendship ('kēṇmai') is compared to the shifting minds of women ('makaḷir maṉam'), which are depicted here as changing easily. Just as those minds lack constancy, the affection of false friends will eventually alter and turn different ('vēṟupaṭum') when circumstances change.
